tasks.text: Last Friday evening Aziz was walking home along the pavement near the old bridge. The traffic was heavy and the noise of the cars filled the whole street. While he was turning the corner, he heard a loud crash behind him. A taxi hit a bicycle, and the driver was shouting at a passenger inside the car. A young man was lying on the road and he could not move his leg. Aziz was carrying his phone, so he called an ambulance immediately. A crowd was gathering around them, but nobody was helping the injured man. Aziz sat next to him and whispered calm words until the ambulance arrived. The next day a police officer thanked him and called him a brave witness.

tasks.text: When I was a child, my family used to live in a small village near the mountains. We did not have a television, so every evening my grandmother would tell us long stories about her own childhood. My cousin and I used to spend the whole summer outside. We would run to the playground before breakfast and stay on the swing until dark. Our neighbour had an old scooter, and he used to let us ride it around his garden. Life was much simpler then. Now I live in the city and I work in an office, so I visit the countryside only twice a year. I still miss those quiet evenings, but I do not miss the strict rules of my grandfather.

tasks.text: Last month Dilnoza travelled to Samarkand for an important meeting. She had booked the hotel two weeks earlier, so she was not worried about anything. But when she arrived at the station, she realised that she had left her documents at home. She called her brother and explained the problem to him. He admitted that he had seen the folder on the kitchen table that morning, but he had not thought it was important. Dilnoza did not blame him, because she had solved harder problems before. She sent clear photos of the documents to the office, and the manager accepted them. Later she confessed that she had never felt so nervous in her life. tasks.text: Nodira has been learning English for three years. She started at a small language centre near her house, and she has been going there twice a week since then. At the beginning she struggled with pronunciation, and she was often exhausted after the evening class. Her teacher told her that patience is more important than talent. Since January she has been practising with a friend from Canada, and her improvement has been steady. She has also been recording her own voice every evening and comparing it with the original. Now she can follow films without subtitles. She has been working on her writing since the summer, because she wants to study abroad next year. Her family says that her determination is the real reason for her success.

tasks.text: The man who lives next door to us is a scientist. His name is Rustam, and he works at the university where my sister studies. He is also the person who helped our neighbourhood build a small library last year. The building which stands behind the market was empty for a very long time. Rustam found a lawyer whose office is in the same street, and together they wrote a letter to a local organisation. Many residents who had never met before started working as volunteers. Today the library, which opens at nine every morning, has more than two thousand books. Rustam says that a community which reads together becomes stronger.
